title: "Maximum Variance Perspective"
description: "Original mathematical teaching with a worked delivery-operations example; MML §10.2."
---

**Study reference:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, §10.2. The examples, reasoning and notation explanations are written independently.

## Start from a problem

If we can retain only one linear coordinate of a centered dataset, a useful choice is the direction along which data vary most. The variance objective leads to an eigenvalue problem.

## Formulate the problem mathematically

$$
\max_{\|\boldsymbol w\|_2=1}\boldsymbol w^\top S\boldsymbol w,\qquad S=\frac1{N-1}X_c^\top X_c
$$

This relation identifies the required structure. Interpret the symbols using the stated model rather than memorising the formula without its assumptions.

## Derive a worked result

Our delivery-feature covariance is approximately [[3.5,1.2],[1.2,0.8]]. A unit direction aligned mostly with distance captures more variance than the item-count axis alone. The maximum achievable projected sample variance is the largest eigenvalue of S.

## Why the mathematics matters

Maximising variance is not automatically maximising predictive usefulness for delivery time. An unsupervised principal direction can discard a low-variance feature crucial to a label.

## Explain or calculate

What variance would the projection onto the distance axis retain? Which covariance diagonal entry tells you?
